01Slot breakout routed

The whole X68000 expansion bus on two ribbon cables: 2 × 50 gold fingers, six SN74LVC8T245 level translators, two 2 × 20 right-angle IDC headers whose shrouds stop 3 mm short of the rear edge, so whatever plugs in sits immediately alongside rather than across a stub of empty board. Plug an FPGA or MCU board on the other end and it becomes any expansion card you like. Built first because it proves the three mechanical unknowns — the finger footprint, the 45° bevel and the card-guide fit — for a few dollars.

Beyond that: there is no schematic, so ERC has never run; the finger geometry is copied from midiori and has never been in a real slot; hard gold and the bevel are order notes that are not in the gerbers; and the BOM's LCSC column is deliberately empty. The full list is in docs/FAB-BREAKOUT.md.

02Logic board netlist only

The other half: the FPGA, its in-package 8 MB PSRAM, the MIDI drivers and jacks, the three rails and the JTAG header. It sits behind the breakout in the same slot — the slot takes 141 mm and the breakout uses 69 — joined by the two right-angle ribbons. Nothing on it touches the X68000 bus directly; the translators all live on the breakout.

Why split the card

Taken together, these two boards are the single-card design cut along the translators. Splitting costs a ribbon and gains the thing that matters while a design is still moving: the bus half is hardest to get right and cheapest to freeze, and the logic half is the one that gets revised. A respin is then a 47-part board, not a 150 mm one.

The same breakout serves a Tang Console on the bench and this board in the machine.

Pin budget, exactly

Parts / nets47 / 87
3.3 V pins (banks 1–2)45 used, 3 free
1.8 V pins (bank 3)15 used, 0 free
Layoutnot started

Bank 3 is full and has to be: it carries the PSRAM, so it runs at 1.8 V, and A1–A15 are the only signals that fit in it.

Which is why the breakout carries two reference voltages Fifteen address lines must arrive at 1.8 V and everything else at 3.3 V, so the breakout's translators split: VREF on header pin 1 feeds data, control and A16–A23; VREF_LOW on pin 3 feeds A1–A15. A host that does not care — a Tang Console, which is 3.3 V only — fits JP2 and ties them together, and then has 48 signals to play with instead of 63. Enough for a MIDI card; not enough for the 8 MB window.

03Single-card alternative on the shelf

What it is

Two MIDI ports on 3.5 mm TRS-A jacks at $EAFA00 and $EAFA10, plus 8 MB of main-memory expansion, on one card — a Gowin GW1NR-9 with its PSRAM in the package doing all of it.

The gateware is finished and tested: real 68000 bus cycles in, decoded MIDI bytes out, 48 pysim tests including a driver probe sequence and an interrupt-acknowledge vector read.

Where it stands

Bank 3 of the QN88P must run at 1.8 V because it carries the PSRAM, and JTAG lives there — which splits the address bus 15 lines at 1.8 V and 8 at 3.3 V, and means the programmer has to drive 1.8 V.

04Slot cover plate drawn

176 × 20 × 2 mm, outline taken from midiori's — a known-good fit — with the hole sizes and positions measured out of their STL rather than guessed. Three 3.5 mm bores at 22 mm pitch; the middle one sits exactly where theirs does, so that one's clearance is proven.
